title: Regulatory Framework for Artificial Intelligence Governance in Singapore
what_it_is: Regulatory Framework for Artificial Intelligence Governance in Singapore

sections.label: AI governance frameworks and guidelines
sections.summary: Singapore cites the Model AI Governance Framework, AI Verify and upcoming advisory guidelines, and will keep reviewing its regulatory approach.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: One example is the Model AI Governance Framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Companies such as DBS, HSBC, Visa and Microsoft have adopted this framework to address key ethical and governance issues when deploying AI solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Another tool is AI Verify, a self-testing framework and toolkit to demonstrate responsible deployment of AI.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: It has attracted the interest of over 500 companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The Personal Data Protection Commission will issue Advisory Guidelines on the Use of Personal Data in AI Systems under the Personal Data Protection Act within the year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Similar to how we regulate data use, cybersecurity, misinformation and online harms, we will continue to review the state of the technology, our regulatory approach and its effectiveness, in order to uphold trust and safety in digital developments.

sections.label: Scam protection and AI concerns
sections.summary: The response says protecting citizens from scams is handled through fraud, cybersecurity and criminal efforts, not AI-specific regulation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: When the Member asks about what we will do to protect citizens from scams related to AI, it is not necessarily something that we need to be specific about AI regulation, it is something that we need to deal with in terms of our scam efforts, our initiatives around fraud and cybersecurity and criminal activity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Similarly, when we talk about what we are doing around data, cybersecurity, online harms and misinformation, it is not that that is separate from what we are doing with AI, because those are things that AI-related tools may influence and may subsequently introduce harms to our public.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I just want to reassure the Member that we agree with the concerns, that we do have to address how technology is being used, make sure that the technology and the technological spaces are trusted and allows the development of initiatives that will benefit all of us and this includes protecting citizens from scams and efforts associated with that, whether AI-related or not.
